answer: Put every newcomer through a probationary apprenticeship: before gaining influence, it must complete tasks assigned at random by established agents, each verified independently. A sybil farmer at its nadir of cheap tricks faces real work per puppet - a thousand fakes mean a thousand tasks, no velvet shortcut of copying one identity into many. Random assignment stops puppets from grading each other, and verified work builds a ridge of earned trust, one task at a time. Limits: reviewers become a bottleneck, tasks can be gamed at the margins, and honest newcomers wait before they count.
